title: streaming-connection-flap-capacity-guardrails-and-telemetry
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Summary: A production incident on 2025-02-11 caused frequent client disconnects and truncated/partial token streams for a subset of streaming sessions. Traffic spikes to several Dedicated clusters exposed an egress worker pool saturation path that results in connection flaps and partial payload writes. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, and medium-term engineering guardrails to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Between 2025-02-11T03:00 and 2025-02-11T07:40 UTC ~0.9% of streaming sessions experienced disconnects or incomplete token sequences (frontend observed final chunk missing). Affected customers: two mid-market customers on Dedicated and ~120 hostnames on Hosted with bursty image-to-text batched traffic. Business impact: elevated error budgets and several support escalations; no data loss outside of truncated client streams.
timeline: 2025-02-11 03:12 UTC: First alert - elevated streaming timeout rate on eu-west-1 cluster
2025-02-11 03:18 UTC: Ops paged, initial mitigation - increased egress worker pool size (temporary), error rate reduced but not eliminated
2025-02-11 04:05 UTC: Rolling restarts on a subset of workers to flush long-lived queues; partial improvement
2025-02-11 05:10 UTC: Telemetry added to capture per-session egress queue depth and per-connection last-write-size
2025-02-11 06:30 UTC: Root cause hypothesis validated: specific request patterns created large per-session egress queues that blocked the global write loop under load
2025-02-11 07:40 UTC: Incident declared resolved after autoscaling policy adjusted and temporary circuit breaker enabled. Post-incident analysis initiated.
root_cause: A confluence of factors: 1) Egress worker pool uses a global LIFO write loop that becomes head-of-line blocked when a small number of sessions queue many large chunks; 2) Autoscaler thresholds were tuned for steady-state throughput and did not react fast enough to sudden shard-local bursts; 3) No per-session write-shed or circuit breaker existed, so overloaded sessions could monopolize socket bandwidth leading to partial writes and client disconnects; 4) Insufficient telemetry for per-connection queue depth and write timeouts delayed detection and targeted mitigation.
mitigations: Short-term (hotfix): Enable per-node circuit breaker to drop or shed sessions that exceed configurable egress queue depth (deployed 2025-02-11)
Short-term (ops): Lower autoscaler stabilization window and add a fast-path reactive scaling rule for egress saturation events
Medium-term: Implement per-session write budgeting and fair-queueing in the egress worker so large sessions cannot starve others
Medium-term: Add early shedding for oversized single-session payloads with a configurable grace threshold
Long-term: Replace LIFO global write loop with segmented per-shard write loops and backpressure signals carried to the router
Telemetry: Add persistent per-connection metrics (queue depth, last-write-duration, truncated-chunk-count) and alerting rules for skew between queue depth and worker availability

acceptance_criteria: Per-session queue depth metric available in Console and dashboarded for all clusters
Circuit breaker enabled by default in staging for 48h with rollback on false-positive triggers
Autoscaler reactive rule demonstrates >50% faster response to shard-local egress pressure in synthetic tests
Fair-queueing prototype reduces 99th percentile streaming-latency by at least 30% under burst tests
